Professor '''Fakhri Al-Bazzaz''' (June 16, 1933 – February 6, 2008) (nicknamed by his students, "Chief") was an [[Iraqi people|Iraqi]]-[[Americans|American]] [[plant ecology|plant ecologist]] specializing in the study of plant community [[ecological succession]]. A professor and prolific author, he was ranked amongst the top ten "Most Cited Scientists in Environment/Ecology, 1992–2002".

==Early years==
Bazzaz was born to a [[Sunni Islam|Sunni Muslim]] family in [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]].<ref name="SimonMattar1996">{{cite book|last1=Simon|first1=Reeva S.|last2=Mattar|first2=Philip|last3=Bulliet|first3=Richard W.|title=Encyclopedia of the Modern Middle East: A-C|url=https://archive.org/details/encyclopediaofmo03simo|url-access=registration|access-date=4 July 2012|year=1996|publisher=Macmillan Reference USA|isbn=978-0-02-897061-5}}</ref> After receiving his bachelor's degree in [[biology]] at [[Baghdad University]] (1953), he received an appointment at Baghdad's Rasafa Education District. His science career was influenced by Baghdad University's biologist Abdul Karim Al-Khudairy and meteorologist Abdul Jabbar Abdullah.<ref name="Grubb2008" /> Bazzaz completed his studies at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] where he received postgraduate degrees (M.Sc.,1960; Ph.D., 1963).<ref name="Foster2010" />

==Career==
He worked at Baghdad University as a lecturer before becoming a professor at the [[University of Illinois]]. At [[Harvard University]], he served as the Timken Professor of Science and the Mallinckodt Professor of Biology. Bazzaz specialized in the study of plant community succession. He was the author of six books and over 200 scientific papers, including an important scholarly paper in 1990 on [[Carbon dioxide]] effects.<ref name="Grubb2008" /> In May 1997, as one of 21 American experts on ecological systems and climate, he co-signed a letter to [[POTUS|President]] [[Bill Clinton]] and [[Vice President of the United States|VP]] [[Al Gore]] regarding global climate change.<ref name="life.illinois.edu">{{cite web|url=https://www.life.illinois.edu/plantbio/history.htm|title=History|publisher=University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaing, School of Integrative Biology, Department of Plant Biology|access-date=4 July 2012}}</ref><ref name="stanford.edu">{{cite web|url=http://news.stanford.edu/pr/97/970603globalwarm.html|title=Ecologists warn President Clinton: Prevent rapid climate change|date=May 22, 1997|publisher=Stanford University|access-date=4 July 2012}}</ref> He was ranked in the top ten of the "Most Cited Scientists in Environment/Ecology, 1992–2002".<ref>Grubb (2008), p. 93</ref> In 2026, the Ecological Society of America established the Fakhri A. Bazzaz & Steward T.A. Pickett Award in honor of his contributions to the field of ecology and his legacy of mentoring the next generation of ecologists, fostering diversity, inclusion and belonging.<ref>{{Cite news |title= |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1127170}}</ref> Bazzaz mentored more than 50 doctoral students over the course of his career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fakhri Bazzaz |url=https://esa.org/giving/endowments/bazzaz-pickett/fakhri-bazzaz/ |url-status=live |access-date=September 10, 2026}}</ref> 

He was elected a Fellow of several organizations: [[Clare Hall, Cambridge#Fellows|Clare Hall of Cambridge University]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], and the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]]. His awards include a [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1988|Guggenheim Fellowship]], the [[Humboldt Prize]], the [[Nevada Medal]], the King Faisal Prize for Biology, a [[Leverhulme Trust|Leverhulme Professorship]],<ref name="Alsabti">{{cite web|url=http://www.naba.org.uk/CONTENT/articles/Obituaries/BazzazF_By_SabtiA.htm |title=Obituary - Professor Fakhri Bazzaz (1933-2008) |last=Alsabti |first=Athem |publisher=National Association of British Arabs |access-date=4 July 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090107093708/http://www.naba.org.uk/content/articles/Obituaries/BazzazF_By_SabtiA.htm |archive-date=7 January 2009 }}</ref> and the UIUC LAS Alumni Achievement Award. He was a founding member of the [[Iraqi National Academy of Science]] in 2003, and was an advisory board member of [[Arab Science and Technology Foundation]] (ASTF);<ref name="Foster2010">{{cite web|url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2010/11/fakhri-a-bazzaz/|title=Fakhri A. Bazzaz Faculty of Arts and Sciences — Memorial Minute|last=Foster|first=David R. |author2=Andrew H. Knoll|author3=James J. McCarthy|author4=Donald H. Pfister|author5=N. Michele Holbrook|date=November 4, 2010|publisher=Harvard Gazette|access-date=4 July 2012}}</ref> the ASTF's Fakhri Bazzaz Award was established in his honor.<ref name="astf.net">{{cite web |url=http://astf.net/en/scientific-research-outlook/77-scientific-research-outlook-2008- |title=Scientific Research Outlook |year=2008 |publisher=astf.net |access-date=4 July 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120206041554/http://www.astf.net/en/scientific-research-outlook/77-scientific-research-outlook-2008- |archive-date=6 February 2012 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bazzaz married the [[biologist]] Maarib Bakri in 1958, and had two children, a daughter Sahar, and a son Ammar. Bazzaz's brother, [[Abd ar-Rahman al-Bazzaz]], served as [[List of Secretaries General of OPEC|OPEC Secretary General]] and [[List of Prime Ministers of Iraq|Prime Minister of Iraq]].<ref name="Alsabti" /> Bazzaz's interests included [[Islamic calligraphy|Arabic calligraphy]] and [[Arabic poetry]]. He died in 2008 in [[Lexington, Massachusetts]], US from [[stroke]] related complications.<ref name="Grubb2008">{{cite web|url=https://docs.google.com/viewer?a=v&q=cache:knX556XX6GIJ:www.planta.cn/forum/download.php%3Fid%3D24788%26sid%3D8da215ce4343d0aa5bd1e0767a4db470+&hl=en&gl=us&pid=bl&srcid=ADGEESi3fsK8kH5_VuH99-GPeJeKuEPDKs4hw6IJzbiW1o5Sizcnnp_tkRCXLiC1GmBH3YtwV2iT6L2n-E8l2lt1K5pVYzmoWj0fcKVHWRUniaIoc-nit_8HpYW8VptOFUUxmTacbbDB&sig=AHIEtbQHRROHH0neoXeN7cwHA9FVddXEdg|title=Resolution of Respect - Fakhri A. Bazzaz 1933–2008|date=April 2008|first=Peter J.|last=Grubb|publisher=Bulletin of the Ecological Society of America|access-date=4 July 2012}}</ref>{{better source|date=August 2025}}
